claims.text: Laser-based additive manufacturing with optimized scan strategies will improve the mechanical integrity of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
Reduced scan speed and interlayer cooling pauses will reduce compositional segregation relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
Reduced scan speed and interlayer cooling pauses will reduce residual stress relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
Reduced scan speed and interlayer cooling pauses will reduce defect formation relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
The intervention will produce a finer microstructure.
The intervention will reduce thermal gradients.
The intervention will produce a more homogeneous elemental distribution.
Slower scan speed and interlayer cooling permit more uniform solidification.
More uniform solidification minimizes compositional segregation.
Slower scan speed and interlayer cooling reduce residual thermal stresses.
Reduced segregation and residual thermal stress lead to fewer cracks and pores.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defects improve mechanical properties.
Laser-AM AlCrFeNiSi will have higher tensile strength than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Laser-AM AlCrFeNiSi will have higher ductility than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Laser-AM AlCrFeNiSi will have at least 20% lower residual stress than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Laser-AM AlCrFeNiSi will exhibit less compositional segregation by EDS mapping than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Laser-AM AlCrFeNiSi will exhibit fewer microscopy-observed defects than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.

The hypothesis is bounded to cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi processed under controlled atmosphere with layer thickness below 50 μm, scan speed below 500 mm/s, and interlayer pauses of 10–30 seconds, followed by room-temperature mechanical testing.
